design_rationale: The study is explicitly described as a randomized controlled trial where participants were randomly allocated using variable block sizes generated by an independent statistician.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated by an independent statistician using variable blocks and concealed using consecutively numbered envelopes handled by independent researchers, with balanced baseline characteristics.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A statistician independent of the research group generated the random allocation, performed in variable block sizes. The random allocation sequences were transferred to consecutively numbered envelopes and were handled by two researchers who were not involved in the data collection or the intervention.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants could not be blinded to the behavioral exercise intervention, and an intention-to-treat analysis was explicitly not performed (only complete cases at 2 years were analyzed), raising concerns for bias in the estimation of the effect of assignment to intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This study did not use intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis, which is commonly used in RCT studies. The decision to exclude ITT analysis was made based on the dropout rate being over 10%...

domain_judgments.rationale: Substantial attrition occurred by the 2-year follow-up (overall ~29% missing data, up to 38% in the OEP group) with complete-case analysis only and no sensitivity analyses or evidence demonstrating that missingness was independent of the true outcomes in this frail older population.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At the 2-year follow-up, there were dropouts in each group: the OEP group included 38 (62%) of the 61 participants who were included at baseline; the OEP+MI group included 42 participants (72%) of the 58 who were included at baseline; and the control group included 44 (79%) of the 56 participants who were included at baseline.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessments were performed using standardized validated tools by assessors blinded to group allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was performed single blinded... Physiotherapists with experience of working with older adults performed the measurements on four occasions: baseline, 3 months, 1 year, and 2 years.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT01778972) and reported the expected pre-specified outcome measures without clear signs of selective outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was registered at clinicaltrials.gov under NCT01778972.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high due to substantial attrition at the 2-year follow-up (up to 38% dropout in an intervention group) coupled with a complete-case analysis approach rather than an intention-to-treat analysis.

design_rationale: The study is a cluster randomized controlled trial where general practitioners were randomly allocated to either the complex intervention or usual care control group using a blockwise randomization list.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although GP cluster allocation was generated by an independent statistician, cluster randomization occurred prior to patient identification and recruitment by unblinded GPs/staff, creating potential identification and recruitment bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was conducted by a blockwise randomization list for both coordination centers, by a statistician who was otherwise uninvolved in the study at the time. Neither the GP nor staff members were blinded to the randomization allocation... After attending the educational workshop, the GPs were randomized either to the intervention or the CG and started to recruit their patients.

domain_judgments.rationale: Due to the nature of the exercise intervention blinding of participants and providers was not possible, but the intervention followed standardized protocols with good fidelity and analyses appropriately accounted for the clustered structure.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Neither the GP nor staff members were blinded to the randomization allocation – blinding for the testing procedure is not feasible in an exercise intervention study... To account for the hierarchical structure in the chosen study design with patients nested in GPs and measurements nested in patients, a three-level linear mixed-effects model was determined for analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Follow-up was obtained for 86% of participants (325/378) with relatively low attrition across both arms (17% in intervention vs 10% in control), and linear mixed-effects models were employed for analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Baseline data (T0) 378 patients: (IG, N = 222) (CG, N = 156)... Drop out T1 IG: N = 27 CG: N = 7 [Erlangen] Drop out T1 IG: N = 11 CG: N = 8 [München]... T1: 325 patients: N = 184 IG, N = 141 CG (usual care)

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors (practice staff) were unblinded to group allocation, and the physical performance tests (e.g. Timed Up and Go, Chair Stand Test, Romberg) and self-reported fear of falling questionnaire (FES-I) are susceptible to assessor and participant expectation bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Neither the GP nor staff members were blinded to the randomization allocation – blinding for the testing procedure is not feasible in an exercise intervention study because participants in the exercise intervention arm would tell their GPs what they were doing... Testing was split between the GPs, who managed medication and chronic diseases, and the trained staff member, who managed the questionnaires and physical performance tests.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered prospectively (NCT01032252) with an earlier published protocol, and outcomes and analyses followed prespecified plans.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study protocol (PreFalls NCT01032252) we used has been previously published and no changes were made.16... In short, it was a controlled, multicenter, prospective study design with an equal cluster, random allocation of participating GPs to a complex intervention or usual care control group (CG).

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high, primarily driven by unblinded outcome assessment (practice staff aware of cluster allocation) on performance and patient-reported measures, alongside potential cluster-recruitment identification bias.

design_rationale: Senior centers (clusters) were randomly assigned to one of four intervention conditions.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study used cluster randomization across 16 senior centers, but the specific sequence generation and allocation concealment methods are not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The 16 senior centers were randomly assigned to one of the four treatment groups (exercise, cognitive-behavioral, exercise-cognitive, discussion control), and all subjects at a center were given the same intervention.

domain_judgments.rationale: An intention-to-treat survival analysis including virtually all randomized participants (229 of 230) was conducted, and no major deviations from the intended interventions were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Thus, all interventions were assumed to start at the day of participants' signing the consent form. The number of fallers during the first year of the intervention did not differ significantly among the groups [log rank chi^2 (3, n = 229) = 2.21, p = .53].

domain_judgments.rationale: Survival analysis for the primary outcome of time to first fall included 229 of the 230 participants, with dropouts tracked and reasons documented.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The number of fallers during the first year of the intervention did not differ significantly among the groups [log rank chi^2 (3, n = 229) = 2.21, p = .53].

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome of falls was measured consistently across all groups using weekly personal or phone contact and monthly diaries, minimizing the risk of differential measurement bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To avoid underreporting, we monitored falls weekly in person or with phone calls and asked for monthly diaries on falls and health status.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcomes prespecified in the methods (time to first fall and severity of injury) are fully analyzed and reported in the results section without indication of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary dependent measures of the investigation were the length of time to first fall and the severity of injury associated with the fall.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to lack of detailed reporting regarding the sequence generation and allocation concealment methods in the cluster-randomization process (Domain 1). All other domains were judged as low risk of bias.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to one of three groups using a computer-developed random table.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated via a computer-developed random table, allocation was concealed from the recruiting assistant, and baseline characteristics were comparable across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The first author used a computer-developed random table to randomly assign patients to three intervention groups: control, CB alone or CB with Tai Chi. Allocation was concealed from the recruiting RA.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although blinding of participants to behavioral/exercise interventions was not feasible, an intention-to-treat approach was used via mixed models accounting for missing data with no apparent non-protocol interventions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Changes in outcome variables at various follow-up times were predicted using a mixed model approach with an intent-to-treat approach whereby all randomized participants were included, and a mixed model was used to account for missing follow-up data.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 10 of 186 participants (5.4%) were lost to follow-up at 5 months, loss was balanced across groups, and dropouts were similar in baseline data with mixed-model ITT analysis applied.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of 186 elderly adults recruited for this trial, 14 withdrew during the 5-month study. Therefore, the final sample consisted of 176 participants (Figure 1). The dropouts and non-dropouts were similar in baseline data (Table 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Assessors collecting outcome data and analyzing outcomes were blinded to group assignment, and validated instruments were used across all groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The RA collecting data, and the second author assessing and analysing outcomes were blind to group assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study does not cite a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified statistical analysis plan, though outcomes reported align with stated study objectives.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The aim of the study was to compare the effectiveness of three interventions (control, CB alone and CB with Tai Chi) on primary outcomes (fear of falling and falls), and secondary outcomes [mobility (gait and balance), social support and quality of life] of community-dwelling elderly adults over 5 months.

overall_summary: The trial was well conducted with computer-generated randomization, allocation concealment, blinded outcome assessment, low attrition, and intention-to-treat analysis; however, absence of a prospective trial registration leads to some concerns regarding selection of the reported result.

design_rationale: The study is a cluster randomized controlled trial where senior centers were randomized to intervention or control using a coin toss.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although a coin toss was used to allocate geographic clusters, details on allocation concealment were not reported, and participants were recruited at senior centers after cluster randomization, introducing potential identification/recruitment bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A coin was tossed to determine allocation between the Brooklyn sites and the South Bronx/Upper Manhattan sites.

domain_judgments.rationale: Both groups received active educational/activity programs delivered by trained staff according to protocol, with no evidence of non-protocol deviations affecting trial outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: control sites received a nutrition course of equal intensity (i.e., an equal number of sessions) to the SESEP.

domain_judgments.rationale: There was substantial attrition (38% overall; 36% in intervention and 41% in control) due to participants simply not attending the single-day follow-up screening, and complete-case analysis was used without imputation or handling of potential bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Follow-up testing included 103 participants (62%), 39 from control sites and 64 from treatment sites. There were no differences in baseline descriptive information between those on whom follow-up data were obtained and those on whom there were no follow-up data.

domain_judgments.rationale: Key outcomes (exercise, physical activity, efficacy, quality of life) relied on participant self-report in interviewer-administered surveys where participants were aware of their intervention group, and outcome assessors were not stated to be blinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Given that this was a community-based study, there were multiple limitations that must be acknowledged. In addition to the selective nature of the sample... the outcomes were all based on self-report rather than objective measures of physical activity... Follow-up data collection days were scheduled 2–4 weeks following completion of the intervention.

domain_judgments.rationale: There was no mention of a pre-registered trial protocol or published analysis plan, leaving some risk of selective reporting across multiple measured outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Given that this was a feasibility study and involved pilot testing of the SESEP, no a priori power analysis was performed.

overall_summary: The study has a high overall risk of bias primarily driven by substantial missing outcome data (nearly 38% lost to follow-up at the 12-week assessment) without appropriate handling for missingness, along with some concerns regarding allocation concealment/recruitment in a cluster trial and reliance on self-reported outcomes without blinding.

design_rationale: The study is described as a prospective, two-group randomized trial where participants were stratified by race and living arrangements and randomized using random permuted blocks prepared with double, opaque envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence generation was random using permuted blocks, concealed using double opaque envelopes, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Study participants were stratified by race (white, nonwhite) and living arrangement (alone, with others) and randomized within each of four strata using random permuted blocks to control for possible changes in subject mix over time. The blocking number, developed by the project statistician (WWH), remained unknown to others. Randomization lists and four sets of randomization were prepared using double, opaque envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Due to the nature of the occupational/physical therapy home intervention, participants were not blinded to their assignment, and no-treatment controls could have introduced behavioral deviations, though treatment implementation was standardized and monitored.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Analyses followed intention to treat such that all subjects providing data were included in analyses regardless of study participation level.

domain_judgments.rationale: Retention was high (94% at 6 months, 89% at 12 months) with reasons for attrition documented and relatively balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 319 participants (159 control, 160 experimental), 300 (94%) were available at 6 months and 285 (89%) at 12 months. Discontinuation of 34 participants by 12 months was accounted for by 14 who died, eight lost to follow-up, five who entered a nursing home, four who were dissatisfied, two who were unable to complete the batteries due to poor health, and one who was hospitalized (Figure 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although interviewers were masked to group allocation, the primary outcomes (functional difficulties, self-efficacy, fear of falling) were participant self-reports, and participants themselves were not blinded to receiving the home intervention versus no treatment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The project codirectors (LW, SS) randomized participants, and trained interviewers who were masked to group assignment and study hypotheses and who had no role in the intervention interviewed them at 6 and 12 months.

domain_judgments.rationale: Analyses followed clearly specified pre-planned ANCOVA models with pre-specified covariates, reporting all primary and secondary outcomes systematically at 6 and 12 months.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Main treatment effects at 6 months were examined using ANCOVA. The outcome measure was the 6-month score with design variables (race and living arrangements) used as covariates for all outcome analyses. To increase precision of treatment comparisons, additional covariates were chosen a priori based on previous research that showed a relationship with outcomes.

overall_summary: Overall, the study has some concerns regarding risk of bias due to lack of participant blinding with subjective self-reported primary outcomes (functional difficulties, self-efficacy, and fear of falling) compared against a no-treatment control group, despite rigorous randomization, allocation concealment, masked assessment interviewers, and low attrition.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized controlled trial in which participants were randomly allocated using computer-generated random block allocation performed by an independent researcher.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, concealed until assignment by an independent blinded researcher, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After baseline measurement, an independent researcher blinded to participant characteristics performed block randomization (two communities x 5 cycles) using a computer-generated random allocation (SPSS 12.0, SPSS, Inc., Chicago, IL).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants were aware of their assignment due to the behavioral nature of the intervention, there were no crossovers and the primary analyses adhered to an intention-to-treat framework using mixed-effects models.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All analyses were performed according to modified intention to treat (i.e., all baseline data and available follow-up data were included)... No participant assigned to the intervention group crossed over to the control group or vice versa.

domain_judgments.rationale: Loss to follow-up was substantial (25% overall) and unbalanced between groups (30.0% in intervention vs 19.6% in control), raising some concern that missingness could bias results despite mixed-effects modeling.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: During the trial, 135 participants were lost to follow-up: 51 (19.6%) of the control group and 84 (30.0%) of the intervention group... Testing for missing completely at random (MCAR) showed that, for all variables except perceived loss of functional independence (P = .02), MCAR was not rejected.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcomes were self-reported by participants who were aware of their intervention group assignment, which could introduce expectation bias despite blinded telephone interviewers.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Outcome assessors were trained centrally on study procedures and were blind to group assignment... At baseline, 2 months... and 8 and 14 months... self-reported data were collected using questionnaires and structured telephone interviews.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (ISRCTN43792817) and reported pre-specified outcomes and analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Further details of this parallel-group randomized controlled trial (ISRCTN43792817) are available... A priori it was specified that all models would be adjusted for baseline values, age, sex, living situation, educational level, cognitive status, perceived general health, and falls history at baseline.

overall_summary: The study was judged to have some concerns overall due to potential bias from differential missing outcome data between groups (30% vs 20%) and the reliance on subjective, self-reported outcomes from participants who were unblinded to their intervention assignment.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized controlled trial in which participants were randomly allocated to study arms using a computerized random-number generator administered by an independent third party.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated using a computerized random-number generator and concealed by an independent third party, with baseline characteristics reasonably balanced across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All randomizations were concealed. (A third party not involved in the study applied a computerized random-number generator.)

domain_judgments.rationale: Due to the nature of exercise interventions, participants could not be blinded, but high adherence protocols were followed, fidelity was monitored, and appropriate mixed-effects models consistent with an intention-to-treat approach were used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All analyses were performed according to a modiﬁed intention-to-treat design (i.e., all baseline data and available follow-up data were included). ... To ascertain ﬁdelity of the interventions, sessions were observed, and monthly supervision meetings were held with the instructors.

domain_judgments.rationale: By 24 months, approximately 26% of participants had missing data, with varying dropout across arms (ranging from 20.5% in MG to 35% in CG), posing some concern for bias despite mixed-effects model analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Complete data sets were available for 207 participants (73.9%) for 24 months, and data were missing for 16 persons (5.7%) at 6 months, for 10 persons (3.6%) at 12 months, and for 47 persons (16.8%) at 24 months. ... Post hoc analyses showed no signiﬁcant baseline differences (P < .05) in age, sex, or number of participants that had fallen in the past 6 months regarding dropout in all groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Assessors administering physical performance tests were blinded to group allocation, and standardized self-report measures and prospective monthly fall calendars were used consistently across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The assessors administering the physical performance tests received training and were blinded to group assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study followed an a priori analytical strategy and systematically reported planned physical, psychological, and fall outcomes across all follow-up time points.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Adjustment of the models for available baseline values of the outcome variables age, sex, living situation, education, fear of falling, and having fallen in the past 6 months was speciﬁed a priori.

overall_summary: The study is well-designed with concealed computerized random allocation, blinded outcome assessors, and an appropriate statistical approach. However, there are some concerns regarding missing outcome data due to 26% overall attrition by the 24-month follow-up with differential dropout rates across intervention arms.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to either the ABLE intervention or fall prevention education using a computer-generated sequence.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence generation was computer-generated, allocation was concealed by an independent colleague until after baseline assessment, and baseline differences were minimal and controlled for in analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was determined using a computer-generated sequence created and held by a colleague with no other connection to the study; the project coordinator obtained the assignment after each participant completed the baseline assessment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial used an active control comparison, fidelity was monitored via videotaped sessions and supervision, and an intention-to-treat approach using mixed-effects models was employed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Intention-to-treat analyses were conducted using repeated measures mixed effects models to examine differences between treatment groups on the outcomes of interest over time.

domain_judgments.rationale: Attrition was very low (9.5% in ABLE, 0% in FPE; 40 of 42 completed), and linear mixed-effects modeling was used to handle missing data appropriately.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two participants dropped out of ABLE (9.5%) after 4 weeks. A total of 40 participants completed treatment and follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors were masked to treatment allocation, and validated standardized measures were used across both groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All assessments were completed by research associates blind to the participants’ treatment condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT01609322), and reported primary and secondary outcomes correspond to the predetermined plan without indications of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All procedures were approved by the local Institutional Review Board and the trial was registered with the National Institutes of Health clinical trials registry (NCT01609322).

overall_summary: The study demonstrated low risk of bias across all RoB 2 domains, with robust concealed randomization, blinding of outcome assessors, minimal missing outcome data analyzed via intention-to-treat, and prospective trial registration.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to one of three study arms using a predetermined block randomization list generated by an independent statistician.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was generated by an independent statistician with variable block sizes and performed by an independent PT after baseline assessments, with no significant baseline differences.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A predetermined randomisation list was made by an independent statistician. Randomisation was performed in blocks to minimise the risk of revealing treatment group membership, with a variable size of three, six, nine or twelve participants.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding of participants and personnel was not possible given the nature of the behavioral/exercise intervention, and participants who dropped out or had delayed intervention were excluded from effect analyses rather than analyzed according to intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Analysed for effect measures, n=13 -excluded from analysis, n=3 [for OEP]; Analysed for effect measures, n=14 -excluded from analysis, n=2 [for OEP + MI]

domain_judgments.rationale: Missing outcome data was relatively low (5/45, ~11%) across groups and reasons for dropouts were documented.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Three-month follow-ups were conducted for 40 participants. [5 participants out of 45 (11%) dropped out or were excluded from effect analyses: 3 in OEP, 2 in MI, 0 in control]

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors were independent physiotherapists who were blinded to treatment group assignment, minimizing potential measurement bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Four PTs performed the measurements single blindly... All measurements were completed in the participant's home or at a health care centre formed by an independent PT who was blinded for group randomisation.

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-specified trial protocol or pre-registration with a statistical analysis plan is cited for this specific feasibility study, raising some concerns for selection of reported analyses/results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The aim of this investigation was to study the feasibility of a randomised controlled trial (RCT)... B) the effects of the intervention programs on fall frequency, physical performance, balance and falls self-efﬁcacy.

overall_summary: The study is judged to have some concerns overall, driven by exclusions from effect analyses without strict intention-to-treat implementation and the absence of a pre-registered statistical analysis protocol for this feasibility report.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized controlled trial in which participants were randomly allocated to one of three groups using variable block sizes and stratified by community.

domain_judgments.rationale: An independent statistician generated the random allocation with variable block sizes, allocation was concealed using consecutively numbered envelopes handled by independent researchers, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The participants were randomly allocated in variable block sizes of 3, 6, 9, and 12 participants to 1 of 3 groups. The randomization was stratiﬁ ed by the 3 communities. A statistician independent from the research group generated the random allocation. The random allocation sequences were transferred to consecutively numbered envelopes that were handled by 2 researchers who did not participate in the data collection or in the intervention.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants and intervention physiotherapists could not be blinded given the behavioral nature of the exercise/MI interventions, treatment fidelity was maintained and analyzed according to the intention-to-treat principle without substantial deviations that would bias the estimated effect of assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The intention-to-treat analysis was complemented with a per-protocol analysis where dropouts and nonadherent participants were excluded.

domain_judgments.rationale: Data were available for 161 of 175 randomized participants (92%), dropouts were low and balanced across groups (7 in OEP, 6 in OEP+MI, 1 in control), and reasons were documented and mainly due to health-related issues.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 161 participants were followed up at 12 weeks: 54 individuals in the OEP group, 52 individuals in the OEP + MI group, and 55 individuals in the control group (Figure). The 14 dropouts during the study period were mostly due to participants’ health-related problems.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessments were conducted by independent physiotherapists who were blinded to treatment group allocation, using validated standard instruments.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The measurements were performed single blinded by 6 independent PTs before randomization and 12 weeks after randomization. All of the PTs had experience working with older people.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was pre-registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01778972) and all primary and secondary outcomes specified in the methods are fully reported according to a pre-defined analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was registered at clinicaltrials.gov under NCT01778972. In this study, the short-term follow-up (12 weeks) is reported, and future follow-ups will occur at 12 and 24 months.

overall_summary: All five domains of bias were judged to be at low risk of bias due to sound randomization with central concealment, blinded outcome assessors, high follow-up rates, intention-to-treat analysis, and prospective trial registration with consistent reporting.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to the control or intervention group using computerized stratified two-block randomization conducted by an external agency.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated via computerized block randomization and concealed by an external agency, with baseline characteristics balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A computerized two-block randomization was performed using the level of concerns about falls (i.e., sometimes, regular, often, and very often) as the prognostic factor. An external agency blinded to participant characteristics conducted the randomization directly after the baseline measurement.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants were aware of group assignment due to the behavioral nature of the trial, an intention-to-treat approach was used, and there were no reported non-protocol interventions or cross-overs that biased the results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Cross-over between groups was not permitted, and participants were aware of their group allocation... Data were analyzed according to the intention-to-treat principle; therefore, all participants were included based on their original allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: There was substantial differential attrition (31% in intervention vs. 17% in control), raising some concerns despite multiple imputation and mixed-effects modeling.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The dropout rates during the trial were 17 % (n = 33) in the control and 31 % ( n = 61) in the intervention group... No significant differences were identified regarding baseline characteristics and primary and secondary outcomes between dropouts in the intervention and control groups. Missing values were imputed at the level of the scale by means of multiple imputations.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors administering telephone interviews were trained and blinded to group allocation, and validated scales were utilized.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Facilitators and participants were aware of group assignments; outcome assessors were blinded to the allocation. Prior to data collection, the outcome assessors from a center for data and information management participated in a 2-hour training session on assessment procedures and study design.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial had a prospectively registered protocol and published study design, and outcomes were analyzed and reported in accordance with the pre-specified plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT01358032. Registered 17 May 2011... Additional information about the study design can be found in a published study protocol [24]. The trial was performed as planned.

overall_summary: The study is judged to have some concerns overall, primarily driven by substantial and differential attrition between the intervention and control groups (Domain 3), despite otherwise robust randomization and blinded outcome assessment procedures.
